result.topic_en: Integration of the separated differential terms gives a relation between two arctangents, which reduces to an algebraic relation between p = dy/dx and u = y/x, after which the remaining differential equation dx/x = du/(p−u) is separable.
result.transcription:
32
evadet $\frac{1}{1+nn}\cdot\frac{\partial t}{tt-\alpha\alpha+\beta}$, cujus integrale erit:
$\frac{1}{(1+nn)\sqrt{\beta-\alpha\alpha}}\cdot\text{Arc. tg.}\frac{t}{\sqrt{\beta-\alpha\alpha}}$, sive $\frac{1}{(1+nn)\sqrt{(\beta-\alpha\alpha)}}\text{Arc. tg.}\frac{p+\alpha}{\sqrt{\beta-\alpha\alpha}}$.
Eodemque modo, loco $p$ scribendo $u$, prioris membri inte-
grale est $\frac{-1}{(1+nn)\sqrt{\beta-\alpha\alpha}}\text{Arc. tg.}\frac{u+\alpha}{\sqrt{(\beta-\alpha\alpha)}}$.
29. Hinc igitur integrale postremae nostrae aequa-
tionis, ob coëfficientes communes, erit:
$C-\text{Arc. tg.}\frac{u+\alpha}{\sqrt{\beta-\alpha\alpha}}=\text{Arc. tg.}\frac{p+\alpha}{\sqrt{\beta-\alpha\alpha}}$,
sive summa horum duorum arcuum aequatur quantitati con-
stanti, consequenter etiam tangens summae horum duorum
arcuum debet esse constans, quae est: $\frac{(p+u+2\alpha)\sqrt{\beta-\alpha\alpha}}{\beta-2\alpha\alpha-\alpha(p+u)-pu}=C$,
unde aequatio ita poterit repraesentari:
$pu+\alpha(p+u)+2\alpha\alpha-\beta=C(p+u+2\alpha)$, sive
$pu-\beta=f(p+u+2\alpha)$.
Quod si hic loco $\alpha$ et $\beta$ valores assumtos restituamus, qui
erant $\alpha=\frac{an}{1+nn}$ et $\beta=\frac{1+aa}{1+nn}$, aequatio nostra erit:
$(1+nn)pu-aa-1=f((1+nn)(p+u)+2an)$.
Ubi notandum est esse $u=\frac{y}{x}$ et $p=\frac{\partial y}{\partial x}$, ita ut haec ae-
quatio adhuc sit differentialis. Ad eam integrandam, cum
posuerimus $y=ux$ et $\partial y=p\partial x$, erit $p\partial x=u\partial x+x\partial u$,
unde colligitur $\frac{\partial x}{x}=\frac{\partial u}{p-u}$. Nunc vero ex postrema ae-
quatione inventa valorem ipsius $p$ per $u$ definire licet,
quo invento aequatio differentialis $\frac{\partial x}{x}=\frac{\partial u}{p-u}$ est separata,
cujus ergo integratio nulla laborat difficultate. Inde igitur

items.english: that is, the sum of these two arcs equals a constant quantity, and consequently the tangent of the sum of these two arcs must also be constant

items.quote:
Nunc vero ex postrema ae-
quatione inventa valorem ipsius $p$ per $u$ definire licet,
quo invento aequatio differentialis $\frac{\partial x}{x}=\frac{\partial u}{p-u}$ est separata,
cujus ergo integratio nulla laborat difficultate.
items.english: Now from the last equation found one may determine the value of p in terms of u; once this is found, the differential equation dx/x = du/(p−u) is separated, so its integration presents no difficulty.
